title: 2017 AMC 8 Problem 10
statement: A box contains five cards, numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5.\) Three cards are selected randomly without replacement from the box. What is the probability that \(4\) is the largest value selected?

solutions.text:
The number of ways to choose \(3\) cards from \(5\) is \({5 \choose 3} = 10.\) If \(4\) is the largest value selected, then the other two cards have to be chosen from \(\{1, 2, 3\}.\) There are \({3 \choose 2} = 3\) ways to do this. The probability is then \(\dfrac{3}{10}.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Count all ways to choose \(3\) cards from the \(5\) cards.
If \(4\) is the largest selected card, the other two selected cards must come from \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3\).
